slides.headline: She grew up in a small Haryana town dreaming of flight. On this day, she left the atmosphere.
On November 19, 1997, Kalpana Chawla launched aboard Space Shuttle Columbia on mission STS-87, becoming the first India-born woman in space.
slides.body: Chawla was born and raised in Karnal, Haryana, where she earned her aeronautical engineering degree at Punjab Engineering College before moving to the US for graduate study. STS-87 was her first of two spaceflights.

slides.headline: A small-town engineering degree carried her all the way to orbit.
slides.body: Chawla logged over 372 hours in space across her two missions. She remains one of the most widely recognized symbols of what an Indian engineering education can lead to, inspiring a generation of students toward science and space careers.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat is still shaped by the ambition of someone who left Karnal convinced the sky wasn't the limit.
slides.body: Chawla's path - small-town India to a Space Shuttle flight deck - is still the reference point for what's possible when that ambition is matched with the right training.
